title: Kotlin/Native Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of kotlin/native fundamentals using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates kotlin/native fundamentals.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Kotlin/Native Fundamentals** as part of **Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, and Kotlin/Native**. Apply kotlin/native fundamentals by identifying the required behavior, the relevant Kotlin type/API, and the conditions under which the expected result can fail. Use the subtopics—Native Compilation, Native Executables and Libraries, Native Platform Toolchains—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-platform targets differ in runtime APIs, toolchains, and support maturity. Check the current compatibility matrix before committing to a production target.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with native compilation. Then compare it with native executables and libraries. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Native Compilation
items.text: Native Compilation is one part of kotlin/native fundamentals. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Native Executables and Libraries

items.title: Native Platform Toolchains
items.text: Native Platform Toolchains is part of reproducible project configuration. Declare the dependency or plugin where it belongs, preserve a compatible version set, and use the Gradle Wrapper for repeatable builds.

content_blocks.code:
data class Greeting(val text: String)

fun greetingFor(name: String): Greeting = Greeting("Hello, $name")

fun main() = println(greetingFor("Kotlin").text)
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run inside a Kotlin/JS, Kotlin/Wasm, or Kotlin/Native project configured for the selected target. Verify platform support and maturity before production use.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Kotlin/Native Fundamentals removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.text: Describe the main rule of kotlin/native fundamentals in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates kotlin/native fundamentals. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving native compilation.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain kotlin/native fundamentals without copying the lesson wording.
Demonstrate the concept with a small code/configuration change and state the expected result.
Test one boundary case or explain a relevant platform/version limitation.
hints: Begin with the first syllabus subtopic: Native Compilation. What input or state does it act on?
Change only one value, branch, declaration, or dependency at a time. Predict what should happen before running the code.
Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
